name: Rotel
impact: Replaces Python logging stack with a single Rust binary OpenTelemetry pipeline; reduces logging CPU and GC overhead versus Python-based collectors
alignment: Rust implementation satisfies Kinetic Purity; single-binary deployment with minimal dependencies satisfies Velocity; can run as a local sidecar without heavy infra, preserving Zero-Burn

name: PRP Templates
impact: Introduces structured Product Requirements Prompts and frozen-context specs that reduce iterative prompt thrash and hallucination risk for large tasks
alignment: Runs as static markdown/templates with no interpreter overhead (Velocity); improves context-density per token by enforcing blueprint-first flows (Enhance); works with local LLM backends (Zero-Burn)

name: MASON
impact: YAML-defined multi-agent workflows proven on small local LLMs, enabling multi-step autonomy without cloud-only dependencies
alignment: No mandatory Python web-stack at runtime when orchestrated via local binaries and small models (Zero-Burn); YAML graph reduces orchestration code-surface, improving Velocity; explicitly designed for local LLMs instead of GPT-4-only setups

name: Saltare
impact: Consolidates all MCP tools behind one low-latency Go gateway, reducing per-tool connection overhead and enabling semantic routing in a single binary
alignment: Pure Go binary aligns with Kinetic Purity; gateway pattern allows single-binary-style deployment at the edge (Velocity); can run locally beside agents without GPU/VRAM requirements (Zero-Burn)

name: Multiagent Debate
impact: Improves factual accuracy and robustness via structured multi-round debate, critique, and consensus among agents
alignment: Protocol, not a heavyweight framework; can be encoded in YAML/JSON and executed on local small models (Zero-Burn); no dependency chains beyond your existing runtime, preserving Velocity; enhances effective reasoning density per token through iterative critique (Enhance)

name: Map-Reduce Swarm
impact: Enables parallel decomposition of large coding/analysis tasks into shards that can be processed by many local agents, then merged into a coherent output
alignment: Topology spec only; can be implemented using Rust/Go orchestrators and small local LLMs (Zero-Burn); focuses on a single orchestrator binary coordinating worker agents, fitting the Law of Velocity; avoids complex interpreter dependency meshes if orchestrated via compiled runner

name: ggRMCP
impact: Wraps existing gRPC microservices as MCP tools via a single Go gateway, reducing the need to re‑implement services while keeping low‑latency, compiled routing
alignment: Pure Go binary aligns with Kinetic Purity; lets you consolidate gRPC services behind one endpoint (Velocity); can run locally without GPU/VRAM needs (Zero-Burn)

name: LocalLLaMA Agent Builders
impact: Provide visual or configuration‑driven workflows for building local‑LLM agents, improving developer ergonomics and enabling multi‑step tasks without cloud dependence
alignment: Designed for local LLMs on consumer hardware (Zero-Burn); generally ship as single binaries or self‑contained apps with limited dependencies (Velocity); can be used as experimental orchestration front‑ends around Camelot’s compiled core
